title: Local recurrence after breast-conserving therapy in multiple ipsilateral breast cancer
journal: Journal of Clinical Oncology 2023; prospective, multicentre, single-arm phase II trial
population: 270 enrolled; 204 eligible patients underwent protocol-directed breast-conserving therapy. Median age 61 years; most had two foci and ER-positive/HER2-negative disease.
treatment: Breast-conserving surgery with negative margins, followed by whole-breast irradiation and boost to each lumpectomy bed; systemic therapy according to tumour biology.
comparator: None; single-arm phase II study. Prespecified acceptable 5-year local recurrence threshold <8%.
summary: At median follow-up 66.4 months, 6 local recurrences occurred; estimated 5-year cumulative local recurrence was 3.1% (95% CI 1.3–6.4). No regional recurrences were reported. Exploratory MRI subgroup: 1.7% with preoperative MRI (n=189) versus 22.6% without MRI (n=15; P=0.002).

absoluteEffect.absoluteBenefit: Not estimable; single-arm study. Observed rate below prespecified <8% acceptability threshold.
absoluteEffect.toxicity: No randomized comparative toxicity endpoint; treatment includes lumpectomy, whole-breast RT and boosts to each tumour bed.

clinicalInterpretation: Z11102 supports breast conservation in carefully selected women with two or three ipsilateral foci after imaging, biopsy confirmation, margin-negative excision and whole-breast RT with boosts. It does not establish randomized equivalence to mastectomy.
criticalReview: The primary analysis included 204 eligible patients and six local recurrences; 5-year cumulative incidence was 3.1% (95% CI 1.3–6.4), below the prespecified 8% acceptability threshold. The MRI comparison was exploratory and highly imbalanced (189 versus 15), so it cannot establish a causal MRI effect. Single-arm design; no comparative NNT.
archiveNote: Previous Trial of the Day after the 8 November 2026 rotation; complete ACOSOG Z11102 analysis preserved.
